title: This Moth Hears Sounds 15 Times Higher Than Humans Can

scenes.text: This moth can hear sounds fifteen times higher than you can.
Humans stop at about twenty kilohertz. The greater wax moth hears up to three hundred.
That's the highest hearing ever recorded in any animal.
Earlier tests stopped at one hundred. Scientists in Scotland kept going, and the moth's ear was still responding.
Scientists think it helps the moth hear bats, which hunt with ultrasound.
Fifteen times higher than you. And it's a moth.

description:
The greater wax moth can hear sounds up to about 300 kilohertz, the highest hearing recorded in any animal.
Humans top out near 20 kilohertz. A 2013 study led by researchers at the University of Strathclyde kept raising the pitch until they hit that limit. Scientists think the moth uses it to hear bat sonar.
What sound do you wish you could hear? Comment below.
first_comment: Dolphins top out around 160 kilohertz. This moth hears almost double that. Which animal should we cover next?
